Article Title: Graham Staines case: SC asks Dara Singh to tweak remission plea for relief hearing
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday granted two weeks to murder convict Dara Singh to challenge the Odisha government's decision rejecting his plea for premature release in the 1999 murder case of Australian missionary Graham Staines and his two minor sons.The top court's decision comes days after the Odisha government pointed out the gravity of the offence and said Singh's plea for premature release had been rejected after considering all facts and circumstances of the case.The top court agreed to hear Singh's petition after three weeks.

Article Title: Operation Sohan: Two terrorists killed in joint operation by Army, CRPF, J&K police in Udhampur
Article Text:
2 terrorists killed in J&K (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: Two terrorists were neutralised during an overnight counter-terrorism operation in Jammu and Kashmir’s Udhampur district, the Army said on Thursday.The operation, code-named Operation Sohan, was launched during the intervening night of September 16 and 17 following confirmed intelligence inputs about the presence of terrorists in the general area of Brattal, the Army’s White Knight Corps said.Despite hostile weather, difficult terrain and poor visibility, troops of the White Knight Corps, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) launched a targeted operation in the area, the Army said.Official said that a joint search operation was launched in the remote Bratel Soan and Khubban areas of Majalta around 9 pm on Wednesday following information about the movement of suspected terrorists.A few rounds of firing and blasts, reportedly carried out by security forces while targeting a suspected hideout, were heard in the forest shortly after the operation began, officials said.The area remained largely quiet through the night before the lull ended on Thursday morning, when the terrorists opened heavy fire in an attempt to break the security forces’ cordon.Security forces retaliated, triggering an encounter that continued in the forested area.The Army later said the operation resulted in the neutralisation of two terrorists. Search and surveillance operations are continuing in the area, while security forces remain deployed to track and neutralise any remaining threat, the White Knight Corps said.The operation comes amid heightened security activity in the Pir Panjal region following the recent busting of an alleged overground worker (OGW) network linked to the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) in Rajouri.On September 15, Rajouri Police arrested three people in connection with an alleged terror module operating in the Pir Panjal region. According to police, the three were allegedly involved in providing logistical support, safe transit and other ground-level assistance to terrorists operating in the region.Preliminary investigation found that the accused allegedly worked as guides and helped facilitate the movement of terrorist groups towards the Kashmir Valley, police said. They were also suspected of providing ground support to terrorists linked to multiple high-profile attacks, including an attack targeting civilians.Police also recovered an improvised explosive device (IED) based on information provided by one of the accused.According to officials, preliminary findings indicated that the IED had allegedly been handed over to the accused by members of a terrorist group for safe custody and possible use in a targeted attack.The recovery of the IED and the arrests have provided investigators with leads into the wider terror network operating in the region, police said.
Article Summary: Two terrorists were neutralised during an overnight counter-terrorism operation in Jammu and Kashmir’s Udhampur district, the Army said on Thursday. The operation, code-named Operation Sohan, was launched during the intervening night of September 16 and 17 following confirmed intelligence inputs.

Article Title: 'See how many allies of Pakistan were in that room': Omar Abdullah praises Centre over Pahalgam condemnation at Brics
Article Text:
Omar praises Centre for Brics

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday heaped praise on the foreign policy of PM Narendra Modi-led Centre and recently held Brics Summit in Delhi. Omar Abdullah said the Brics declaration condemning Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack was a major diplomatic win.J&K CM remarks came after India hosted the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi, bringing together several world leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The National Conference leader particularly highlighted the inclusion of the Pahalgam terror attack in the Brics New Delhi Declaration, pointing out that the statement came in the presence of countries that share close ties with Pakistan."That is something for the Government of India, and particularly for the foreign ministry, to talk about. The fact that Pahalgam itself was condemned is a big thing. Please see how many allies of Pakistan were in that room. Therefore, for even Pahalgam to be mentioned by name, that in itself is a success of our foreign policy," Omar Abdullah said.J&K CM Omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along India’s fronts with Pakistan and China.Reacting to the ministry of defence’s report on the operational situation along the Northern Front, he said any move to reduce troop deployments along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) or Line of Control (LoC) would be a positive development, particularly for people living in border areas."Anything that reduces tension along the Line of Control or the Line of Actual Control is a good step, particularly for those people who live close to it. We know that living near the LoC or LAC is extremely difficult for people. If there is any step that reduces deployments along the Line of Actual Control, that is a good step. Similarly, we hope that, over time, things will also get better along the Line of Control," he added.The comments came days after the Brics Summit concluded in the national capital. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the New Delhi Declaration had been unanimously adopted and called the gathering as a huge summit.Days ago, senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor backed the Brics Summit as an important diplomatic opportunity for India, appearing to differ with party colleague P Chidambaram, who questioned whether recent Brics meetings have produced tangible benefits.Tharoor highlighted the diplomatic value of India hosting leaders from across the Brics grouping and its partner countries, stressing the importance of such engagements for New Delhi.Chidambaram, however, had questioned the outcomes of recent Brics summits.“I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results.”“In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics Summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Chidambaram’s remarks triggered a political response from the BJP, which accused the Congress of questioning an event that, it said, reflected India’s growing standing on the global stage.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah heaped praise on the foreign policy of PM Narendra Modi-led Centre. He said the Brics declaration condemning Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack was a major diplomatic win. Omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along India's fronts with Pakistan and China.

Article Title: ‘Umar Khalid is a nationalist’: B K Hariprasad’s remark sparks BJP attack
Article Text:
Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a nationalist.





BENGALURU: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad Tuesday called jailed activist Umar Khalid a “nationalist” and criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University (NLSIU).“ABVP has no right to speak about Khalid because ABVP adores Nathuram Godse, who is anti-national and the first terrorist of the country,” Hariprasad said.The remarks came after ABVP in Bengaluru demanded cancellation of the proposed screening of filmmaker Lalit Vachani’s documentary, ‘Prisoner No. 626710 is Present’, at NLSIU. The documentary was scheduled to be screened Monday by the law and society committee, a student organisation at the university. NLSIU later said it had to reschedule the event due to “logistical and security considerations”.The screening was to express solidarity with Khalid and to mark six years since his imprisonment without trial under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in connection with the 2020 Delhi riots.BJP hit back at Hariprasad’s remarks, calling them deeply condemnable. In New Delhi, Sambit Patra, MP, linked Hariprasad’s remarks to Congress’ past interactions with Kashmiri separatist leader Yasin Malik.“Just think about it: this is the same Umar Khalid,” Patra said. “During the Citizenship Amendment Act protests in Feb 2020, so many people were killed in Delhi. A case was filed under UAPA. The matter was heard across multiple courts; even in Feb 2026, the Supreme Court rejected Umar Khalid’s bail plea. Look at the sympathy Congress party harbours for the very same Umar Khalid.”Patra also attacked Congress party over its meetings with Yasin Malik, alleging the party had reduced itself to “appeasement”.
Article Summary: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a ‘nationalist’ He criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University.

Article Title: Maratha activist Jarange Patil calls off 20-day fast, gives govt 3 months to consider demands
Article Text:
Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike.

NEW DELHI: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange Patil on Thursday called off his 20-day-old hunger strike and gave the Maharashtra government three months to consider his demands, news agency PTI reported.The decision came after Jarange addressed a large gathering at Patoda in Beed district around 2 am, raising concerns about his worsening physical condition and the possibility of abandoning his planned march to Mumbai.Jarange, who had entered the day 18 of his fast at the time of the address, said he was too physically exhausted to continue a long journey with thousands of supporters travelling behind him.He asked Maratha community members not to follow his vehicle after he left Patoda. Instead, he urged them to meet him directly at Khopoli. He warned that if the convoy continued, he might stop the journey and resume his sit-in protest in Patoda or return to Antarwali Sarati.Despite reaching the venue at around 1.30 am, Jarange found thousands of people, including women, waiting to hear him speak.Addressing the gathering, he said he could barely move his limbs after stopping IV fluids on September 12."Fighting for the children of my community has taken a toll on my body, but I have taken on the government for you. The government wants me to surrender, but should I abandon our demand? My community is greater than any government - it is my father. My community holds the power to bring down any government and install a new one," he asserted.Jarange said the movement had made progress after 58 lakh archival records, known as nondi, were uncovered. He claimed these records could help nearly 2.5 crore members of the Maratha community access reservation benefits.He said the immediate demand was for the Maharashtra government to issue an official gazette recognising the relevant records.The activist also criticised chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, claiming he had countered the government's political moves and that all the documented records had been secured on pen drives. He further accused Fadnavis of "plotting against his life".Responding to the government's argument about fruit orchard owners in Western Maharashtra, Jarange questioned why OBC communities that also own orchards should not receive reservation benefits."The government claims Western Maharashtra has fruit orchards, but don't OBC communities own orchards too? Why do they have a reservation then?"Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike. He appealed to supporters to avoid following his vehicle and said he would prefer to travel directly to Mumbai from Patoda after speaking to the police, if his health allowed.He also spoke about his family, saying he had asked them to live with self-respect and told his son to remain courageous if he died for the community."I have told my family to live with self-respect. I told my son to step up courageously if I give my life for the community. Let one life be sacrificed for the cause, but never let the dignity of our caste be lowered," he said.
Article Summary: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange Patil called off his 20-day-old hunger strike. He gave the Maharashtra government three months to consider his demands. Jarange said he was too physically exhausted to continue a long journey with thousands of supporters travelling behind him. He asked Maratha community members not to follow his vehicle after he left Patoda.

Article Title: Pak vessel PNS Hunain damaged after collision with Indian warship in North Arabian Sea, returns to harbour
Article Text:
PNS Hunain of the Pakistan Navy has returned to harbour after severe damage

New Delhi: In another incident of friction, a Pakistan navy ship collided with an Indian warship when the latter was on a routine surveillance mission. The incident happened on Tuesday evening in the North Arabian Sea.“On the evening of Sept 15, a Pakistan Naval Ship closed a frontline Indian Naval warship on a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea at high speed, manoeuvring in an unprofessional and unsafe manner. This led to a collision,” a source told TOI, adding, “No damage has been reported”.“The Pakistani naval vessel involved in the collision was PNS Hunain of the Pakistan Navy. It has returned to harbour after severe damage,” the source told TOI.“Even under extreme provocation, the Indian warship’s captain exercised extreme restraint by taking actions to prevent a severe accident from taking place, which could have caused serious loss of lives and damage,” the source said.PNS Hunain (F273) is the third ship of the Yarmook-class corvettes operated by the Pakistan Navy. It was built by the Dutch shipbuilder Damen Shipyards at its Galai shipyard in Romania.New Delhi has summoned Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires (CDA) after the incident. “The CDA was summoned to the Ministry of External Affairs today and a strong protest was lodged with him over the unacceptable and unprofessional conduct of Pakistani naval units at sea that led to a collision with a unit of the Indian Navy ," the MEA said.The MEA said the diplomat was advised to convey to the Pakistani authorities concerned the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents. New Delhi stated the approach breached Article 10 of the April 1991 bilateral agreement on advance notice for military exercises, which mandates a minimum three-nautical-mile distance between the two navies' units.This is not the first time a Pakistani naval vessel has collided with an Indian warship. On June 16, 2011, Pakistani naval vessel PNS Babur “brushed past” Indian frigate INS Godavari in the Gulf of Aden, triggering a diplomatic row. PNS Babur was escorting Egyptian-owned merchant vessel MV Suez, which had been freed after Somali pirates held it hostage for several months. A helicopter net of INS Godavari was damaged when PNS Babur moved closer to the Indian warship while coming from behind.
Article Summary: Pakistan navy ship collided with an Indian warship when the latter was on a routine surveillance mission. Incident happened on Tuesday evening in the North Arabian Sea. New Delhi has summoned Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires (CDA) after the incident.

Article Title: 'There's no Pak-China boundary': India tells Islamabad to drop 'theatrics', vacate occupied territory
Article Text:
India rejects the so-called Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday rejected the so-called Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission, saying it has no legal basis and reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India.Responding to media queries, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson said, "We have seen reports in this regard. Our position on this matter is clear and consistent. There is no boundary between Pakistan and China. We reject the so-called Joint Commission, which is without any legal basis."The MEA said the entire Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh "have been, are and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India"."Pakistan has no locus standi to enter into arrangements concerning Indian territory under its illegal and forcible occupation," it said.India also reiterated that it has never recognised the so-called "China-Pakistan Boundary Agreement" of 1963 and has consistently maintained that it is "illegal and invalid"."We resolutely oppose and reject any attempts to alter the status of these occupied territories or legitimise illegal occupation, impinging on India's sovereignty and territorial integrity," the MEA said.It added that any "so-called boundary cooperation" between China and Pakistan concerning Indian territories would be "completely unacceptable" and would have no bearing on India's sovereignty over those territories."Instead of engaging in such theatrics, we call on Pakistan to immediately vacate from areas under its illegal and forcible occupation," the MEA added.In recent years, China has maintained military pressure along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with India, with border violations and unauthorised entries reported across all three sectors of the 3,488-km-long boundary between the two countries.The coordination between China and Pakistan along the border in the Karakoram region of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, which stretches over 590 km, also impacts India's historical and legal claims over the area.
Article Summary: India rejects the so-called Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission. It says it has no legal basis and reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India. India also reiterated that it has never recognised the "China- Pakistan Boundary Agreement" of 1963.

Article Title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
Article Text:
Earlier, the Bombay HC ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Salian's death.

Bombay HC orders CBI probe

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following an order of the Bombay high court.No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.The FIR names several individuals whose roles have been listed for investigation, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty , Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The document also names former state home minister Anil Deshmukh, several police officers, forensic officials, doctors and other individuals.“The then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya Thackeray, and others also played a significant role in the conspiracy and subsequent cover-up. The concerned public servants and police officers are also liable to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders,” the FIR stated.The FIR said the listed individuals would be investigated in connection with the alleged principal offences, criminal conspiracy, the “subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story” and the alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.It also named officers associated with Malvani Police Station, doctors and staff involved in the post-mortem, officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory in Kalina, security guards of Regent Galaxy Building, members of the special investigation team and other unidentified persons.Earlier this month, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI investigation into Salian’s death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years.The court observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than answers”. The bench also questioned the decision to treat the case only as an accidental death and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation.Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) in the case.Salian had briefly worked as Sushant's manager. The actor was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death.The proximity of the two deaths triggered widespread speculation about a possible link, although the cases were investigated separately.Following the public uproar over Rajput’s death, the Maharashtra government ordered a CBI probe. The agency later submitted a closure report stating that Rajput had died by suicide. The report, however, is yet to be heard by the court concerned.Earlier, Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had accused Aaditya Thackeray and actor Dino Morea in connection with his daughter’s death.Speaking to ANI on Friday, Satish Salian said he had told investigators what he knew about the events surrounding his daughter's death and provided names of several individuals whom he wanted authorities to examine.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down. They said they would take action based on what I told them; the proceedings would begin in a few days,” he said.“The truth cannot be defeated. God stands where the truth is; that is why justice will be served,” he added. Mumbai Police had earlier maintained, after its inquiry, that Salian had died by suicide.
Article Summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian. No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.

Article Title: 'Why are you afraid of Umar Khalid?' Congress dares PM Modi & Shah to move court

NEW DELHI: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge on Wednesday alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were "afraid" of jailed student activist Umar Khalid and challenged them to conduct his trial."Why are they (BJP government) not bringing up the trial? It's been so many years that he's in jail; there are apparently some charge sheets on him. Why is the trial not going on? Why are they (BJP) so afraid to conduct the trial? Mr Modi and Amit Shah, why are you so afraid of Umar Khalid? Take action," Priyank said, as cited by PTI."Who is telling Mr Umar Khalid is anti-national? Has the court said that? BJP is telling he's an anti-national. BJP tomorrow will tell you that you are an anti-national. Do we have to believe that?" he added.Kharge advised the ABVP to focus on more constructive activities and said the student organisation should take up issues such as education reforms with the Union government."Talk about the education reforms that youngsters, the Gen Z, are talking about. Talk about the KPSC scam that your (BJP) leaders are involved in. Why are you behind Umar Khalid? He's in jail.How is he harming you? Convict him. Who's saying no? But why is ABVP indulging in all these things about which documentary to be shown, which documentary not to be shown? This kind of goondaism will not be tolerated," he said.Khalid was arrested in September 2020 in connection with the larger conspiracy case related to the February 2020 Delhi riots and was booked under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, among other provisions. Kharge questioned why the trial had not yet commenced.The development comes a day after Karnataka Congress president BK Hariprasad described Khalid as a "nationalist" and criticised the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) over its demand for the permanent cancellation of a proposed documentary screening on the jailed activist at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU).Hariprasad also questioned the student organisation's moral authority to comment on Khalid."Umar Khalid is a nationalist, and ABVP has no right to speak on him because they adore Nathuram Godse—who was an anti-national and the first terrorist of the country. They have no moral right," Hariprasad said.The remarks came after the RSS-affiliated student organisation sought the Centre's intervention to permanently cancel the proposed screening of the documentary Prisoner No. 626710 is Present, directed by Lalit Vachani, at NLSIU.The screening was recently postponed by the organisers, who cited security and administrative reasons. In a statement on Monday, ABVP Bengaluru said it had submitted representations to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi and Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal, seeking their intervention.The organisation also called for a high-level inquiry into the NLSIU administration over the proposed screening.
Article Summary: Karnataka home minister questions delay in Umar Khalid's trial. Priyank Kharge challenges Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah to conduct his trial.Khalid was arrested in September 2020 in connection with the larger conspiracy case related to the February 2020 Delhi riots.

Article Title: Tejashwi targets Centre, says ‘no money for flood-hit, but lamps for PM’s birthday’
Article Text:
Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav inspects flood-affected areas from a bridge to assess the ground situation, in Bihar. =

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav on Wednesday hit out at the Centre over the flood situation in Bihar, alleging that the government had no money for flood-affected people but was ready to spend on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday celebrations."Govt has no money for the flood-affected people but they are ready to spend for PM's birthday by lighting lamps," Yadav said.His remarks came amid the ongoing flood situation in parts of Bihar affecting nearly 50 lakh people across 15 districts of the state. Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month, about six per cent above normal, according to the local weather office.Earlier in the day, BJP appealed to people to light an ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ at their homes on September 17, marking Modi's birthday. BJP president Nitin Nabin, Union minister Kiren Rijiju and other party leaders have made the appeal through social media.The lamp-lighting initiative is part of the BJP's month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’, which includes service activities, welfare outreach and public-participation programmes across the country.
Article Summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav hit out at the Centre over the flood situation in Bihar. He said the government had no money for flood-affected people but was ready to spend on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday celebrations. Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month.

Article Title: 'Callous and criminal conduct': Delhi HC on Satya Niketan building collapse that killed 7
Article Text:
Delhi HC calls the incident 'callous and criminal' conduct

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Wednesday said the collapse of a multi-storey hostel building in Satya Niketan, which killed seven people including students, was "not an ordinary incident. "A bench of Chief Justice D K Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said four students who died had come to Delhi from small towns with hopes of building their careers. The court said their dreams were “shattered” because of the “callous and criminal conduct” of certain persons.“Four students lost their lives in the mishap...very tragic. It's not an ordinary incident of any mishap. These four students had come to the capital with a lot of hopes and dreams, coming from small towns. All of that was shattered by such callous and criminal conduct on the part of (certain persons),” the court said.The building, which housed a boys’ paying guest accommodation near Delhi University’s South Campus, collapsed on September 6 while repair work was under way. Several people were injured in the incident.Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma told the court that authorities had taken several steps after the collapse, including mapping and identifying land and other facilities that could be used by students.The bench, however, said the shortage of hostel facilities in Delhi was not a “new phenomenon”.“Who doesn't know the problem of hostels in the city? Students are flocking to Delhi for higher education, and this is not a new phenomenon. It has been happening for the last 20-25 years in the hope that they will build their career. See what has happened,” the bench said.The court was hearing a PIL filed by Aakarshak Danveer Rathi seeking an independent probe into the collapse, inspection of all paying guest accommodations and a compensation and rehabilitation scheme for victims and their families.The high court said it would hear the PIL along with another pending petition on September 25.On September 7, the court had ordered a high-level MCD inquiry into the collapse and said the government could not evade responsibility.It had also said the incident raised serious concerns over inadequate housing and hostel facilities, student safety and the measures taken by the MCD and other authorities to regulate paying guest accommodations.
Article Summary: Delhi HC calls the incident 'callous and criminal' conduct of certain persons. Court was hearing a PIL filed by Aakarshak Danveer Rathi seeking an independent probe into the collapse, inspection of all paying guest accommodations and a compensation and rehabilitation scheme for victims.

Article Title: 'Special significance to Muslims': India condemns Houthi drone attack near Saudi Arabia's Mecca
Article Text:
India condemns drone attack on Mecca

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday condemned the drone attack near Mecca in Saudi Arabia, saying the incident was particularly concerning because of the city’s importance to Muslims worldwide.The ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, responding to media queries, said: “We are deeply concerned at the drone attack near Makkah. India reiterates its condemnation of attacks on the sovereign territory of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and of actions that endanger civilian lives and infrastructure. The incident near Mecca is particularly concerning, given the special significance of the city to Muslims across the world. ”“We hope for the early restoration of peace and stability in the region,” Jaiswal added.Also read: 'Nauseating lie': Houthis deny targeting Mecca; claim strike on Saudi F-15 Saudi Arabia said its air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it could enter the holy city’s restricted airspace.Saudi military spokesperson Turki al-Malki called the safety of the holy sites and pilgrims as a “red line” and warned of measures against the Iran-backed Houthis.The Houthis, however, denied targeting Mecca. Houthi spokesperson Hazem al-Assad wrote on X: “The claims about targeting Mecca are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone.”Mecca is home to the Kaaba and is the destination of the annual Haj pilgrimage. Muslims around the world face the Kaaba while offering prayers. Saudi Arabia’s role as custodian of Islam’s holiest sites is central to its position in the Muslim world.The alleged attack comes as Saudi Arabia faces growing pressure from the Houthis, who have stepped up attacks on the kingdom and its interests in the Red Sea. Iran, which backs the Houthis, has also been targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz.A key Saudi oil pipeline has reportedly remained shut for weeks amid attacks on infrastructure. The disruption has added to concerns for the world’s biggest oil exporter as shipping through Hormuz remains under pressure.
Article Summary: India condemns drone attack on Mecca in Saudi Arabia. Ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: "We are deeply concerned at the drone attack near Makkah" Saudi Arabia said its air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca.

Article Title: MPSC paper leak: CJP to join protesters demanding resignation of key officials, sets Sept 24 deadline
Article Text:
Abhijeet Dipke, the party founder, confirmed his backing after engaging with the aspiring candidates

CJP threatens statewide tour

Abhijeet Dipke backs MPSC aspirants' demands





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) and its founder Abhijeet Dipke will join MPSC aspirants protesting alleged paper leaks and irregularities in online examinations conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission, the party said on Sunday.The CJP has also set a September 24 deadline for its demand seeking the resignation of the MPSC chairman and secretary.The announcement followed a meeting between a group of MPSC aspirants and Dipke at his residence in the Waluj area of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The CJP said the agitation demanding the resignation of the MPSC chairman and secretary would continue.If the two officials did not step down by September 24, Dipke and party members would undertake a statewide tour to meet MPSC aspirants and take up their concerns, the party said in a release.Dipke and other CJP members will also participate in the ongoing protests by MPSC aspirants, it said.After meeting the aspirants, Dipke said in a video message, "The CJP and I are with MPSC aspirants in this fight. We will stand with the aspirants till the resignations (of top MPSC officials)."MPSC aspirants have held protests at several places across Maharashtra , seeking greater transparency in the recruitment process and action over alleged paper leaks and other irregularities in various examinations conducted by the commission.The protests have centred on demands for accountability and transparency in the conduct of MPSC examinations.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party and its founder Abhijeet Dipke will join MPSC aspirants protesting alleged paper leaks and irregularities in online examinations conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission. The CJP has also set a September 24 deadline for its demand seeking the resignation of the M PSC chairman and secretary.

Article Title: US extends visa curbs on Palestine officials, blocks President Abbas from UN General Assembly
Article Text:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas appears on a screen as he addresses the 80th United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)

The United States has extended visa restrictions on Palestinian Authority officials and members of the Palestine Liberation Organization, preventing President Mahmoud Abbas and other Palestinian officials from travelling to the US ahead of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.According to Reuters, the US state department said it had determined that the Palestinian Authority and PLO continued to engage in actions that Washington considers inconsistent with commitments made under US laws. The restrictions come ahead of the annual UN gathering, where Palestinian statehood and the Israel-Palestinian conflict are expected to remain major issues.The state department said the Palestinian leadership had continued to pursue measures against Israel through international bodies, including the International Criminal Court and the International Court of Justice. Washington also cited efforts to secure international recognition of a Palestinian state outside negotiations with Israel.The US has previously said such actions violate commitments made by the Palestinian Authority and PLO under the PLO Commitments Compliance Act of 1989 and the Middle East Peace Commitments Act of 2002. The administration also cited what it described as payments to individuals involved in terrorism and the glorification of terrorism.The restrictions are tied to two US laws governing Palestinian commitments. The PLO Commitments Compliance Act of 1989 requires Washington to assess whether the PLO is meeting commitments on recognising Israel, accepting UN resolutions and renouncing violence.The Middle East Peace Commitments Act of 2002 similarly requires the US to assess compliance by the PLO and Palestinian Authority with commitments made during the Oslo peace process, including resolving outstanding issues through negotiations and peaceful means.The restrictions will prevent Abbas and other affected Palestinian officials from travelling to New York for the UN General Assembly. The US imposed similar visa restrictions last year, and the latest decision extends those measures ahead of this year’s UN session.The state department said the restrictions do not apply to Palestinian officials covered by a waiver for the Palestinian Mission to the UN. The waiver allows accredited Palestinian diplomats to enter the US and participate in UN-related activities despite the broader visa restrictions.The US decision comes as the Palestinian leadership faces growing diplomatic pressure over its international campaign for recognition of statehood and legal action against Israel. Washington has repeatedly opposed efforts to pursue Palestinian statehood through international forums rather than through direct negotiations with Israel.
Article Summary: US state department said it had determined that the Palestinian Authority and PLO continued to engage in actions that Washington considers inconsistent with commitments made under US laws. The restrictions come ahead of the annual UN gathering, where Palestinian statehood and the Israel-Palestinian conflict are expected to remain major issues.

Article Title: 'Oh it's a she': Trump stops speech to address woman, tells her 'mother watching on TV furious'
Article Text:
President Donald Trump speaks during a campaign rally at the Gastonia Municipal Airport, in Gastonia. (Photo: PTI)

Trump campaigns for Michael Whatley

Trump has used the ‘mom’ line before

US President Donald Trump paused a campaign rally in Gastonia, North Carolina, on Wednesday after a woman interrupted his speech, saying she was “going home to mama” before resuming his remarks.Trump initially appeared to assume that the person interrupting him was a man. “Let me see his face,” he said while looking towards the disturbance, before realising the protester was a woman. “Oh, oh, it’s a ‘she.’ Hello!” he added.“She’s going home to mama — who’s watching right now. Her mother is watching right now on television, furious at the daughter,” Trump said.The exchange was captured in a video posted by Fox News from the Gastonia rally.Trump was speaking at Gastonia Municipal Airport while campaigning for Republican US Senate nominee Michael Whatley, a former chairman of the Republican National Committee who is running against former Democratic North Carolina governor Roy Cooper.The November 3 contest is for the seat being left open by Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who is not seeking re-election. Trump has backed Whatley as Republicans seek to retain the North Carolina seat.Trump also used the Gastonia rally to attack Cooper and Democrats on crime and public safety as he sought to bolster Whatley’s campaign.The Gastonia appearance was Trump’s first major campaign stop since the Republican Party’s midterm convention in Dallas last week. Trump has promised more campaign appearances ahead of the November 3 elections and urged supporters in North Carolina to treat the contest as though he were running himself, telling them to “pretend that I’m on the ballot”.The Gastonia exchange was not the first time Trump has responded to a rally interruption by suggesting that the protester would have to answer to their mother — before adding that the mother supported him.At a January 2020 rally in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, a protester interrupted Trump’s remarks. “Now she’s going home to mom where she will be in big trouble,” Trump said, before adding: “Because I guarantee you that mom voted for Trump.”Trump used a similar line during his 2016 presidential campaign. After a protester interrupted a rally in Erie, Pennsylvania, he told the person to “go back home to your mama” before adding: “your mother is voting for Donald Trump.”Together with the Myrtle Beach exchange last month, the earlier incidents show that Trump has returned to the same mother-themed response to protesters at rallies across different election cycles.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump paused a campaign rally in Gastonia, North Carolina, after a woman interrupted his speech. Trump initially appeared to assume that the person interrupting him was a man. “Oh, oh, it’s a ‘she’ Hello!” he added.

Article Title: ‘Inshallah’: How remarks in UPSC video landed Bengal IPS officer Bushra Bano in soup
Article Text:
IPS officer Bushra Bano was transferred from Kharagpur to state armed police.

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the backlash received by Bushra Bano for her video? It is justified It is an overreaction 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





KOLKATA: A video by IPS officer Bushra Bano, in which she spoke about her UPSC journey and referred to Aligarh Muslim University ’s Residential Coaching Academy, has drawn criticism on social media, days before she was transferred from her post as additional SP of Kharagpur.Bano, a 2021-batch IPS officer, was transferred on Monday as deputy commandant of the state armed police.In the video posted on September 13, Bano spoke about how AMU’s Residential Coaching Academy helped her prepare for the UPSC examination. She began the video with “Assalamualaikum”, used “Inshallah” while speaking about her journey and ended with “Jazakallah”.The video subsequently drew criticism from several users on X, who questioned why she had not used expressions such as “Jai Hind” or “Vande Mataram”.The X handle Hindu Legal Fund claimed it had complained to the Bengal home secretary over the video. In its complaint, the handle alleged that a serving officer representing the Indian state should maintain neutrality in public communication and use national expressions.Bano’s transfer order did not publicly cite the video or the social media criticism as the reason for the move.As part of the reshuffle, Partha Ghosh was appointed additional SP of Kharagpur, while Subhendu Mondal was transferred as additional deputy commissioner of Chandannagar Police Commissionerate.

In the video posted on September 13, Bano spoke about how AMU’s Residential Coaching Academy helped her prepare for the UPSC examination.
