Article Title: Jarange’s Mumbai stir: Health concerns grow after 18-day fast; Fadnavis flags protest timing
Article Text:
Jarange accused govt of repeatedly failing the Maratha community and vowed to continue the agitation.

— with inputs from Chaitanya Marpakwar & Abhishek Choudhari





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange on Tuesday began his march from Antarwali Sarati in Jalna district to Mumbai, setting the stage for another showdown with state govt. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed for a protest that does not disrupt Ganeshotsav.Eighteen days into his indefinite hunger strike, Jarange left his Jalna village around noon and announced that he would resume his fast at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan on Sept 19. His convoy is expected to travel more than 400 km through Beed, Ahilyanagar, Pune and Raigad before reaching the state capital.The march comes amid uncertainty over permission for the proposed protest. Mumbai Police have already rejected two applications seeking permission for an indefinite hunger strike at Azad Maidan. A fresh application, this time seeking permission for a gathering of 50 people and assuring compliance with all conditions, remains under consideration.Addressing reporters on Tuesday, Fadnavis said, “Police had rejected Jarange’s application seeking permission to protest in Mumbai. Police will decide on any fresh application based on its merits.”The chief minister maintained that govt had already addressed most of the movement’s demands.“Govt has accepted 12 of the 13 demands raised by the Maratha protesters that were legally valid,” Fadnavis said, adding that legal constraints prevented action on the remaining demands.“I feel that instead of taking such a position during the festive days, they should take a decision so that people do not face any inconvenience,” he added.Jarange, however, accused govt of repeatedly failing the Maratha community and vowed to continue the agitation.“I will not surrender before govt,” he said, adding the protest was aimed at securing justice for Maratha youth and future generations.Earlier in the day, Jarange underwent a health check-up, offered prayers at a Hanuman temple and then set out with a small convoy of supporters. Crowds gathered along the route, raising slogans and greeting the activist. The response slowed his movement considerably, with the convoy covering barely 22 km in nearly six hours before heading towards Patoda in Beed district.Concern over Jarange’s health continues to grow. He has reportedly stopped accepting medical treatment and saline after police denied permission for the Mumbai protest. His supporters fear his condition may worsen during the journey.His wife, Sumitra Jarange, blamed govt for forcing him back onto the streets. “Govt is incapable of understanding us. If they had taken decisions earlier, he would not have set out for Mumbai. When every person has the right to agitate, how can the govt deny permission for our agitation?” she asked.The state has deployed a Special Protection Unit officer and a constable to accompany Jarange throughout the march.Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde , speaking publicly on the issue for the first time since the Mumbai agitation was announced, said, “Govt is taking care that Ganesh devotees do not face any inconvenience. Earlier, 58 morchas were held, and the world took note of those morchas. No one was ever inconvenienced or allowed to face any inconvenience through those morchas. Therefore, we want everyone to ensure that no one is inconvenienced during Ganeshotsav,” Shinde said.The Jarange agitation was also discussed at Tuesday’s cabinet meeting. Minister Shambhuraj Desai defended the administration’s handling of the issue, saying it had honoured commitments made during talks with the activist and had undertaken extensive work to trace Kunbi records through the Justice Shinde Committee.OBC groups and MoS Ashish Jaiswal too backed govt’s stand on Jarange’s agitation on Tuesday, arguing that most of his demands have already been met and accused him of prolonging a now “non-issue” movement. However, NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar blamed govt for failing to engage meaningfully with the Maratha quota activist.MoS Ashish Jaiswal said govt had established the required scrutiny mechanism for Maratha reservation claims and that grievances should be addressed through legal channels rather than street protests. He alleged that Jarange’s continued agitation was being driven by “malice and prejudice” and was creating unnecessary confusion.OBC Mahasangh president Babanrao Taywade said most of Jarange’s demands had been fulfilled except those pending before courts. He argued that the agitation was unlikely to receive public support and accused Jarange of holding people hostage to a protest.Rohit Pawar, however, said govt was responsible for the impasse. He argued that the lack of sustained dialogue had pushed Jarange back onto the streets and questioned the police decision to deny permission for a protest in Mumbai. “Holding a protest is a constitutional right,” Pawar said.
Article Summary: Eighteen days into his indefinite hunger strike, Manoj Jarange left his Jalna village around noon. He announced that he would resume his fast at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan on Sept 19. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed for a protest that does not disrupt Ganeshotsav. Jarange accused govt of repeatedly failing the Maratha community.

Article Title: Long waits, costly rides: DTC contractual drivers on strike, buses stay put in depots
Article Text:
Bus services across Delhi faced disruptions Tuesday as contractual drivers initiated a strike.

Many buses remained parked at depots, affecting commuters significantly.





NEW DELHI: Bus services in several parts of Delhi were disrupted Tuesday after drivers employed through private agencies for Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) went on strike , demanding higher wages and medical and social security benefits.The strike affected operations at several areas such as Burari, Paschim Vihar, Mundka, Rewla Khanpur, Nehru Place and Shadipur. A large number of buses remained parked inside the depots.The protesting drivers work under a contract with DTC. Representatives of DTC Karmachari Ekta Union, which called the strike, said the contractual drivers are paid lower wages than permanent DTC employees.They also do not get social security, medical insurance, paid leave or an annual bonus, the union said. Drivers with 10-15 years of experience continue to be treated as unskilled workers for wage purposes, the union claimed.By the union’s estimate, around 12,000 contractual drivers work for DTC. Manoj Sharma , general secretary of the union, said the drivers are paid Rs 747 per day. He said the union was demanding at least Rs 2,000 per day. “Our demand is that the salary should be increased. We want the salary to be at least Rs 60,000,” Sharma said.Permanent DTC drivers were paid more than Rs 70,000 a month along with other facilities, he claimed. The union had raised the absence of medical benefits and paid leave several times as drivers go unpaid if they become ill, he added.The union said the strike would continue till the demands were met. Union members claimed that half the drivers are with them and more would join in the coming days. The union was open to talks if its demands on wages, medical cover and social security were addressed.Asked about the strike, transport minister Pankaj Singh said: “These are not DTC workers, but staff employed by our concessionaires. I have asked the concessionaires to look into their demands. They are our brothers. If they have any problems, they should communicate with us instead of going on a strike. We don’t want the people to face any problems. If the concessionaires are not agreeing to their demands, we are ready to help them. But if people are still troubled, we will take necessary action. ”Many commuters had to take the metro and try for app-based autos and cabs. Some reported long waits at bus stops. Metro stations in some areas also saw higher crowds.Shivam Sejwal, a resident of Lado Sarai, said he waited for more than an hour at Nehru Place, after which he decided to take an auto. “Even the auto charged me Rs 300, which is a lot higher than the normal rate.”
Article Summary: Bus services across Delhi faced disruptions Tuesday as contractual drivers initiated a strike. The strike affected operations at several areas such as Burari, Paschim Vihar, Mundka, Rewla Khanpur, Nehru Place and Shadipur. Many buses remained parked at depots, affecting commuters significantly.

Article Title: DUSU elections: ABVP, NSUI trade allegations of attacks and intimidation ahead of polls
Article Text:
The ABVP and the NSUI have traded allegations of attacks and intimidation involving their members and candidates





NEW DELHI: With Delhi University set to vote for its students’ union on September 18, the ABVP and National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) have traded allegations of attacks and intimidation involving their members and candidates, with both student organisations demanding police action.In a press statement, the ABVP alleged that NSUI workers entered the residence of its members at Hari Mandir in Delhi and attacked them while they were holding a meeting.It said women student members were also present at the residence when the alleged incident took place.The ABVP alleged that several individuals fled the spot after the alleged attack, while one person was apprehended by its members and handed over to the police. It further claimed that the apprehended person admitted to being part of NSUI’s social media cadre.ABVP Delhi State secretary Sarthak Sharma said, "NSUI must explain why its workers reached the residence of ABVP members and attacked them despite women student activists being present there. ABVP members were holding a peaceful meeting and had not provoked anyone. One person who was fleeing after the attack was apprehended and handed over to the police.ABVP did not take the law into its own hands; instead, we handed the individual over to the police. ""The apprehended person has admitted to being part of NSUI's social media cadre. Congress-IYC-NSUI must explain why its social media cadre was involved in an attack on the residence of ABVP members? Students of Delhi University can clearly see the difference between democratic student engagement and the use of violence. ABVP members are continuously engaging with students peacefully, while people associated with Congress-IYC-NSUI are allegedly resorting to violence," he alleged.Sharma further noted, "The Congress leadership must clarify its political accountability for the activities of its youth and student organisations. ABVP will not be intimidated by violence or pressure. We demand an impartial police investigation and strict legal action against all those involved, along with adequate measures to ensure the safety of students. The facts of the incident can also be verified from the local police. "The NSUI, meanwhile, alleged that ABVP workers attacked the residences of its DUSU candidates Vijay Shankar Meena and Gopal Choudhary. It alleged that nearly 200 ABVP workers were involved in targeting and intimidating its candidates.NSUI Media Incharge Ravi Pandey said, "This is a desperate attempt to create fear and violence just before the DUSU elections. We demand immediate intervention and strict action by the Delhi Police to ensure the safety of our candidates and students. Such hooliganism cannot be allowed in a democratic student election.""ABVP knows that students are ready for change. On September 18, Delhi University students will answer this politics of intimidation through their democratic vote," he added.The NSUI, in its statement, appealed to the Delhi Police and university authorities to take immediate steps to ensure peace and security during the election process.The allegations come amid heightened tensions on the Delhi University campus in the run-up to the DUSU polls.On the final day of campaigning, separate clashes and allegations of violence were reported at multiple locations, with ABVP and NSUI also trading accusations over some of those incidents.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: The ABVP alleged that NSUI workers entered the residence of its members at Hari Mandir in Delhi and attacked them while they were holding a meeting. The NSUI, meanwhile, alleged that ABVP workers attacked the residences of its DUSU candidates Vijay Shankar Meena and Gopal Choudhary.

Article Title: Bombay high court denies bail to teen in fatal car crash case, cites need to curb spoiling children
Article Text:
Bombay high court denied bail to a teen accused in a fatal car crash





MUMBAI: Observing that it was “necessary to curb activities that spoil children and cause a threat to society,” Bombay high court declined to grant bail to a teen accused of rashly crashing his father’s car into a scooter in Feb.The scooterist, businessman Dhrumil Patel, died 10 days later while undergoing treatment for his injuries, while his wife, the pillion rider, became permanently disabled.The collision occurred close to midnight on Feb 5 at Vidyavihar. Police arrested the teen, then aged 17 years and 8 months. On March 6, a magistrate at Juvenile Justice Board in Dongri granted bail to the minor, which the sessions court, in an appeal filed by the injured victim, set aside.The teen challenged the bail cancellation before HC. Dismissing his plea, a single-judge bench of Justice Shivkumar Dige at HC in a Sept 9 order, available on Wednesday, said he was as good as 18 years old—an adult and “though he is a student, keeping him in a reformative home would make him understand gravity of his act.”HC said though while on bail he was to stay in Navi Mumbai, during an enquiry, the police did not find him there nor did he contact the cops, thus showing his “scant respect for the orders.”Advocate Jitesh Jadhav for the teen sought bail saying the crash was not intentional, it “happened suddenly” and considering his age and that he is a student, no purpose would be served by keeping him at an observation home.In his reasons to not cancel the bail, Justice Dige said, “When he was a child, there was no parental control over him” and he “would be exposed to moral, physical and psychological danger due to the lack of parental control. He may again indulge in a stunt act with his friends, causing danger to others. It will defeat ends of justice.”Besides, HC noted, the stunt videos are deleted from the teen’s Instagram account, which amounts to destruction of evidence, and his friend has been charged with the offence.Advocates Atharva Dandekar and Ruben Mascarenhas for the widow and B B Kulkarni, a prosecutor, opposed the grant of bail arguing the boy had a “habit of performing stunts on bikes and cars” on public roads, which was dangerous to the public.HC said screenshots of the stunts from social media show how he put not only his own but the health and safety of others at risk.Justice Dige said, “Resultantly, one person has lost his life and other became completely paralysed” for no fault of theirs. “Sessions Judge has passed a well-reasoned order, therefore no interference is required in it,” HC held and dismissed the teen’s plea.
Article Summary: Bombay high court declines to grant bail to a teen accused of rashly crashing his father’s car into a scooter in Feb. The scooterist, businessman Dhrumil Patel, died 10 days later while undergoing treatment for his injuries. His wife, the pillion rider, became permanently disabled. Police arrested the teen, then aged 17 years and 8 months.

Article Title: 'Rs 3.5L supari’: Delhi school teacher hires contract killers to murder wife, stays out of city
Article Text:
A government teacher and two associates were arrested for plotting his wife's murder.





NEW DELHI: A 28-year-old govt school teacher and two associates have been arrested for allegedly plotting to kill his wife and orchestrating a shooting at their residence in Baprola, west Delhi , police said.The woman sustained multiple gunshot injuries in the Sept 13 attack and is undergoing treatment at a hospital in Dwarka. Her condition is stated to be stable.Police identified the accused as Sandeep Kumar (28), a resident of Baprola Vihar and husband of the victim, Mitthu alias Deepak (26) of Najafgarh, and Akash (26) of Nand Nagri.According to investigators, Sandeep allegedly plotted the attack following prolonged marital disputes. Police said Deepak and Akash entered the woman’s house in Nangli Dairy on the pretext of collecting or repairing a printer. After spending nearly 45 minutes inside, Akash allegedly opened fire at the woman while she was on the staircase.Police said multiple rounds were fired and three bullets struck the victim before the two accused fled.A case was registered at Ranhola police station under Sections 109(1) (attempt to murder) and 3(5) (common intention) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with provisions of the Arms Act.During the investigation, police arrested Deepak and Akash. Their interrogation allegedly revealed that the shooting had been carried out at Sandeep’s behest, following which he was arrested.Investigators alleged that Sandeep struck a deal worth Rs 3.5 lakh to eliminate his wife and deliberately stayed out of Delhi on the day of the attack to avoid suspicion. He had allegedly informed his wife that two men would visit the house to collect or repair a printer.Police said Deepak and Akash had agreed to carry out the attack in return for money. Sandeep allegedly paid them Rs 1 lakh in advance, with the remaining amount to be paid later.Police said marital discord had existed between the couple for several years.
Article Summary: A 28-year-old govt school teacher and two associates have been arrested for allegedly plotting to kill his wife. The woman sustained multiple gunshot injuries in the Sept 13 attack and is undergoing treatment at a hospital in Dwarka. Police identified the accused as Sandeep Kumar (28), a resident of Baprola Vihar.

Article Title: From Konkan to Karachi: Marathi tradition of Ganeshotsav celebrated across the border, too
Article Text:
Marathi-speaking families in Pakistan celebrate Ganeshotsav with enthusiasm.

TOI

TOI





PUNE: Their ancestors moved from the Maratha heartland to the north during the Third Battle of Panipat circa 1761. Centuries later, after the Partition of 1947, the Marathi-speaking families of many of these travellers’ descendants remained settled in Pakistan . And, even today, they have managed to retain the connect to their Marathi roots. This year, nearly 700 Marathi-speaking Pakistani nationals are celebrating Ganeshotsav in the lanes of Karachi city amid much fanfare.On the first day of the festival, chants of “Ganapati Bappa Moraya” echoed as devotees took out a procession on a 5km stretch from Karachi’s Punjab Colony to Ratneshwar Mahadev temple. This year, the younger generation of Karachi’s Naik family, which has its roots in Maharashtra’s Konkan region, made a 5-ft tall Ganesh idol for the very first time.“We deliberately involved the youngsters in the idol-making process, so that they remain connected to our community’s religious traditions even while staying on this side of the border. From children to senior citizens, all members of our family participated in the activity. We are happy that we could install a 5-ft Lord Ganesha idol this year,” said Mukesh Naik, a member of the Marathi-speaking community of Karachi.The Naik family originally hails from Konkan, where Ganeshotsav has been feted in a traditional manner for centuries. Some members of their family moved to northern regions during the British rule in undivided India. After the Partition, they settled in Pakistan. For generations now, the Naiks have furthered the custom of celebrating Ganeshotsav with others in the community around them.Many such Marathi-speaking families connect with each other socially in Karachi under the umbrella of the Maharashtra Panchayat. Vishal Rajput, another such Marathi-speaking Pakistani national, toldon a call, “We want to keep our Marathi traditions alive while living in Pakistan. So, we celebrate every festival of ours — particularly Ganeshotsav — with much enthusiasm. Hundreds of community members here take part.”He added, “For the first time in our history, we are celebrating the festival for seven days at Karachi’s Ganesh Math Mandir. We conduct a daily aarti, distribute modaks and other Marathi traditional sweets as prasad, and will take out a procession with Lord Ganesha’s idol in the city.”Community members said they have expanded this festival’s celebrations in the last few years, including Sindhi and Punjabi-origin residents for the revelry. Organisers said it takes around one month to complete preparations ahead of the festivities.Vinod Daultram, another Marathi-speaking Karachi resident, told, “Preparations begin with the beginning of the month of Shravan. While managing our daily work, we take out some time for idol-making, decorations and prasad preparations.”“This year’s 5ft-tall Ganesha idol was made in the span of a single month. Sculpting the face was the most difficult part. Since we did not have many references in Karachi, we took the help of social media and finally managed to bring out a beautiful idol,” Vinod added.Suman Naik, another Karachi resident, said preparing for this festival felt akin to serving the deity for her. “I painted the Ganesha idol for the first time, and I felt proud that I got the opportunity to connect with our religious tradition and serve god. Younger generations of our community in Pakistan should show enthusiasm for participating in such celebrations to remain connected to their roots.”
Article Summary: This year, nearly 700 Marathi-speaking Pakistani nationals are celebrating Ganeshotsav in the lanes of Karachi city amid much fanfare. This year, the younger generation of Karachi’s Naik family, which has its roots in Maharashtra's Konkan region, made a 5-ft tall Ganesh idol for the very first time.

Article Title: Allahabad high court frees man to live with Muslim partner after conversion row
Article Text:
Allahabad high court on Wednesday freed a 31-year-old Shamli man, saying he is at liberty to live wherever and with whomever he chose





SHAMLI: Allahabad high court on Wednesday freed a 31-year-old Shamli man, saying he is at liberty to live wherever and with whomever he chose after he alleged that his father had kept him under illegal restraint over his conversion to Islam and decision to marry a Muslim woman.HC held that "an adult's choice of religion and life partner is protected by Constitution and cannot be overridden merely because it is unacceptable to his family".Justice Sandeep Jain passed the order on a habeas corpus petition filed by Ayush Malik's friend, Sultan, who had alleged that Malik was being unlawfully confined by his father, Devraj Singh Malik, with the connivance of police.HC had termed the allegations "serious" on Sept 9 and directed state authorities and Devraj to produce Malik before it, following which a sub-inspector from Kotwali police station, Shamli, brought him to court on Wednesday.Malik told HC that he was a BPharma graduate and had voluntarily embraced Islam in 2014 without coercion, pressure or inducement, and had since followed the faith despite his parents' opposition."I embraced Islam of my own free will and I want to marry Chandni Qureshi. Nobody has forced or pressured me," he told HC, while alleging that he had been threatened and kept under house arrest since June 4.The dispute had earlier led Devraj to lodge an FIR at Kotwali police station on June 6 against Qureshi, her relatives and others under Uttar Pradesh Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, 2021, along with provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Qureshi and her father, Islam Qureshi, were arrested in the case and remained in jail until District and Sessions Judge, Shamli, granted them bail on July 24.Devraj disputed his son's version before HC and maintained that Malik had been "influenced or brainwashed", saying he opposed both the conversion and proposed marriage because he did not believe they were in his son's interest.Justice Jain said Malik, being an adult, was competent to make decisions concerning his faith, residence and marriage and found no material to disbelieve his statement.Invoking Article 25 (freedom of conscience and religion) and Article 21 (life and personal liberty) of Constitution, HC held that there was no lawful justification to continue any restraint on him.The court allowed Malik to reside wherever and with whomever he chose, practise the religion of his choice and take decisions regarding marriage in accordance with law, and disposed of the habeas corpus petition.
Article Summary: Allahabad high court on Wednesday freed a 31-year-old Shamli man, saying he is at liberty to live wherever and with whomever he chose. Ayush Malik alleged that his father had kept him under illegal restraint over his conversion to Islam and decision to marry a Muslim woman. Malik told HC that he was a BPharma graduate and had voluntarily embraced Islam in 2014.

Article Title: Health deteriorates, but Manoj Jarange to head straight to Mumbai
Article Text:
Manoj Jarange will travel directly to Mumbai from Patoda on Thursday.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange on Wednesday altered his march plans and announced he would travel directly to Mumbai from Beed’s Patoda on Thursday. Doctors, however, advised him against travelling and warned that his deteriorating health could turn critical.On the 19th day of his indefinite fast, Jarange said he would leave for Mumbai at 1pm, abandoning the planned route through Ahilyanagar and Pune.His decision came hours after doctors found his blood pressure and blood sugar levels had dropped sharply and diagnosed severe dehydration. Beed civil surgeon Dr Satish Solanke advised immediate hospitalisation. Jarange took saline and drank water, saying he did so on the request of the mahant of Shankargad.The activist, however, remained defiant. “Even if death comes, I will not step back. Whatever happens to me, the fight for Maratha reservation will continue. I will leave for Mumbai at 1pm tomorrow,” he said.Jarange had halted at Patoda after becoming too weak to continue to his next scheduled stop at Shrigonda. Earlier in the day, he acknowledged the physical strain of continuing the march while fasting.“Travelling during a fast is difficult. Reservation is important, not the journey. To reach Khopoli, a person needs to be able to eat,” he said.The activist said ministers, including Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil, were expected to meet him in Patoda but made it clear that talks would be meaningful only if they addressed the community’s demands. “Ministers should come only if they are coming to fulfil the demands of Marathas,” he said.The standoff intensified as Maratha protesters in Nanded threatened to stop the guardian minister from hoisting the national flag on Marathwada Liberation Day. Protesters also briefly blocked the Patoda-Beed highway.Meanwhile, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed to Jarange to call off the march and seek treatment, saying govt had already accepted 12 of his 13 demands.“His agitation has continued for several days and is affecting his health. He should get admitted and take treatment. The agitation can continue later, but his health is important,” Fadnavis said.Jarange, however, rejected suggestions that he would retreat and warned against any attempt to stop the march. “I will go to Mumbai. Let me see who stops me. If we are stopped, lakhs of Marathas will reach Mumbai,” he said.He also asked supporters accompanying his convoy to return to their villages, saying he would call them if the administration tried to block the march.As political tensions rose, Jarange renewed his demand for implementation of the Shinde committee recommendations and sought clarity on the Hyderabad and Satara-Kolhapur gazette issues linked to Maratha reservation.
Article Summary: Jarange halted at Patoda after becoming too weak to continue to his next scheduled stop at Shrigonda. Doctors found his blood pressure and blood sugar levels had dropped sharply and diagnosed severe dehydration. Jarange took saline and drank water, saying he did so on the request of the mahant of Shankargad.

Article Title: 6 years on, gangster Vikas Dubey is officially dead
Article Text:
The Kanpur Nagar Nigam issued Vikas Dubey's death certificate on September 11, nearly six years after his police encounter





KANPUR: Kanpur Nagar Nigam issued the death certificate of gangster Vikas Dubey, the main accused in the Bikru case, on Sept 11, about six years after he was killed in a police encounter.Dubey died in Kanpur on July 10, 2020, but his death certificate could not be issued because his father’s name was incorrectly recorded in the panchnama and cremation slip. Instead of Ram Kumar Dubey, his father’s name was entered as Raj Kumar Dubey.His wife, Richa Dubey, approached several officials before filing a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court seeking the certificate. Following directions from the High Court, the health department investigated the matter.Chief medical officer Dr Hari Dutt Nemi visited the post-mortem house as part of the inquiry, after which the certificate was issued.Nagar Nigam sources said the certificate was sent by registered post to the Bikru address provided by the court. It was widely circulated on social media after reaching the village.Richa told the court that Dubey was not considered dead in the official records, preventing the nominee from receiving benefits under an insurance policy in his name.His property and land could also not be transferred to his heirs.On July 2, 2020, a police team went to Bikru village in Chaubepur police station area to arrest Dubey. Its vehicles were blocked with a JCB, and gunmen opened fire from rooftops as personnel approached his house.Eight policemen, including a circle officer, were killed. UP police and Special Task Force subsequently killed six criminals linked to the case in encounters.Rajesh Singh, zonal officer of Zone 4, Nagar Nigam, confirmed on Wednesday that the certificate had been issued and sent by registered post.
Article Summary: Dubey died in Kanpur on July 10, 2020, but his death certificate could not be issued because his father’s name was incorrectly recorded in the panchnama and cremation slip. His wife, Richa Dubey, approached several officials before filing a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court seeking the certificate.

Article Title: ‘They’re my family’: Bengaluru woman stops crowd from attacking men accused of kidnapping her
Article Text:
Locals attacked a car on Magadi Road, suspecting a kidnapping attempt





BENGALURU: High drama unfolded on Magadi Road Wednesday night after a group of locals allegedly thrashed several men and damaged their car, suspecting they were trying to kidnap a young woman.Six persons, including a nine-year-old girl, sustained injuries in the commotion.However, the alleged kidnapping took a dramatic turn when the woman intervened and told the crowd that the men were her own family members, including her father, who had come from Rajasthan to take her back home.Speaking to police who arrived at the spot, the woman said she had married a man from another caste despite her family’s opposition. She alleged that her family had recently traced her to Bengaluru and was trying to force her to return to Rajasthan.“I’ve married a man from another caste and my family was against it. Recently, we came here and my family somehow followed me,” she told police.A senior police officer said the woman was being requested to lodge a complaint against her family so that action could be taken.Meanwhile, the family’s vehicle was badly damaged after the crowd attacked it. The family members allegedly tried to flee the spot, ramming into other vehicles in the process, officials added.Of those injured, one woman with serious head injuries has been shifted to the ICU of a nearby private hospital, police added. Cops said they are yet to register a case. Suspects have been detained and the car used in the “kidnapping” seized, police said.
Article Summary: Six persons, including a nine-year-old girl, sustained injuries in the commotion. The woman said she had married a man from another caste despite her family’s opposition. She alleged that her family had recently traced her to Bengaluru and was trying to force her to return to Rajasthan.

Article Title: Mahua Moitra faces egg-attack in West Bengal's Tehatta
Article Text:
Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra faced an egg attack in Tehatta while attending a party meeting





TEHATTA: Eggs were thrown at Trinamool Krishnanagar MP Mahua Moitra in Tehatta on Wednesday after she arrived in her constituency to attend a party meeting.Moitra alleged that seven to 10 BJP workers, including the local mandal president and the president and vice-president of the panchayat samiti, threw eggs at her after she came out of the first meeting of the day, even as police stood watching.On Sept 1, Calcutta High Court had directed police to deploy two personnel for a month to protect Moitra during her visits to her constituency, where eggs and stones have been pelted at her repeatedly since her party’s defeat in the assembly elections.On Sept 9, Moitra had written to Krishnanagar SP Atul V regarding her visit to Tehatta from Sept 15 to 17. On Sept 11, the SP wrote back stating she had been assigned a lady assistant sub-inspector to act as the nodal officer for her visit.Moitra did not face any trouble while reaching the meeting venue in Tehatta 1 block. The local inspector in charge, Supriya Ranjan Maji, however, claimed he was unaware of any meeting.In a video message posted on X, Moitra could be heard saying: “We are at Tehatta party office. You can see, we are under police protection, and the court has said no one will throw eggs. They brought eggs right in front of the police. Look at this, all of you.What is happening? Right in front of the police, they are trying to throw eggs… this is contempt of the high court.”“According to the court’s direction, four police personnel were with me. During the attack, more cops came, but instead of controlling the protesters, they forcibly put me into the car. This is what is happening in West Bengal! The high court has been saying this should not happen,” she added.At one point, Maji approached the MP, telling her to leave immediately while questioning why he was not informed about the meeting. Moitra told the officer that it was an indoor meeting and that she had arrived only after receiving the SP’s assurance.As Moitra boarded her SUV, she was hit with two eggs. Refusing to back off, she kept shouting slogans. Her nodal officer was seen pushing away an attacker who had approached her vehicle.Moitra headed to her next meeting, with broken eggshells stuck in her hair and her face smeared with egg.“It is important that people see what is happening in Bengal today. An MP is being attacked with police doing nothing. And this is after a Calcutta HC order. But if they think they can intimidate and scare me, or my party workers off, they have picked the wrong person and the party. We will continue to fight. And when the right time comes, they will have to pay back,” the MP said.In a statement, Moitra also referred to the Supreme Court’s observations while dismissing her plea seeking protection from such attacks.Denying his party’s involvement, Bengal BJP spokesperson Debjit Sarkar said, “Eggs being pelted at a woman… I condemn it if the claims are true. At the same time, it has to be seen whether she has made it all up. I don’t think BJP workers were involved in it.”
Article Summary: Eggs were thrown at Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra in Tehatta on Wednesday. She was attending a party meeting in her constituency. Calcutta High Court had directed police to deploy two personnel for a month.

Article Title: Jhiram Ghati attack: NIA court sentences 10 Maoists to death
Article Text:
A special NIA court has delivered a severe sentence to ten Maoists, condemning them to death for their role in the notorious 2013 Jhiram Ghati ambush





RAIPUR: A special National Investigation Agency NIA ) court in Chhattisgarh's Jagdalpur Wednesday sentenced 10 Maoists to death for their involvement in the 2013 Jhiram Ghati ambush in Bastar.The Jhiram attack took place when Maoists blocked the Congress convoy in the Darbha area and launched a coordinated ambush. It became one of the most consequential Maoist attacks in Chhattisgarh, wiping out several senior Congress leaders in a single strike.According to the NIA's official case records, 27 people, including 10 police personnel, were killed and 38 injured when Maoists ambushed the Congress Parivartan Yatra convoy in Jhiram valley on May 25, 2013.Among those killed were then Chhattisgarh Congress president Nand Kumar Patel and his son Dinesh Patel, former leader of opposition Mahendra Karma and former MLA Uday Mudliyar. Former Union minister Vidya Charan Shukla, who was critically injured, died later.Special NIA judge Ajay Singh Rajput pronounced the punishment Wednesday. The Special Judge convicted the accused under several provisions of the (IPC), Arms Act, Explosive Substances Act and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.The court handed down the death penalty under Section 120B (criminal conspiracy) and Section 302 (murder) of IPC.The 10 convicts are Pramila Modiyam, Chaitu Lekam alias Munna, Sumita alias Punem Modiyam, Mukka Mandvi, Kosa Kavasi alias Kosaram, Aayata Markam, Madkami Deva, Joga Madkami, Banjami Sanna alias Chamru, and Mahadev Nag.One accused died during the trial, and 28 others named in the chargesheet remain wanted. A total of 101 prosecution witnesses were examined during the trial and several documentary pieces of evidence were presented.The ambush occurred on May 25, 2013 near the Bastar-Sukma border. Over 150 Maoists targeted the 20-vehicle convoy, killing Salwa Judum founder Mahendra Karma, state Congress chief Nand Kumar Patel, his son Dinesh, and former MLA Uday Mudliyar.
Article Summary: A special National Investigation Agency NIA court in Chhattisgarh's Jagdalpur Wednesday sentenced 10 Maoists to death for their involvement in the 2013 Jhiram Ghati ambush in Bastar. 27 people, including 10 police personnel, were killed and 38 injured when Maoists ambushed the Congress Parivartan Yatra convoy on May 25, 2013.

Article Title: 900m buffer zone earmarked in Gurgaon, but not even 9m gap between houses and IAF ammo depot
Article Text:
Illegal developments spread around Gurgaon Air Force depot





GURGAON: The 900-metre restricted zone around Indian Air Force’s ammunition depot in old Gurgaon has been almost entirely built over, with multi-storey houses standing virtually flush against the facility’s boundary wall, leaving little to no buffer between habitation and a sensitive defence installation. Supreme Court on Tuesday criticised state officials for colluding with local land sharks to allow this encroachment. The depot was established in 1947.Fifteen illegal colonies have come up in the belt over the years, turning it into a dense urban pocket of kothis built cheek by jowl along narrow lanes.Residential buildings, PG accommodations, shops, schools, factories, cloud kitchens and commercial establishments now fill the zone. In several stretches, no open space separates the built-up area from the depot wall.Five- to seven-storey buildings have come up close to the installation, giving occupants elevated vantage points overlooking the depot — effectively erasing the physical buffer the restricted zone was meant to preserve.The affected pockets include Sheetla Colony, Rajiv Nagar, Sanjay Gram, Sukhrali Enclave, Ashok Vihar Phase 3, Om Vihar, Dharam Colony, Amanpura and Caterpuri, among others.The 900-metre zone covers roughly 2,325 acres.During Tuesday’s hearing, CJI Surya Kant said the no-go zone was earlier more than a kilometre and it gradually reduced to 900 metres, and even then, the illegal constructions were carried out right under the nose of the officials. “Are the encroachments not because of the collusion of govt officials with the land mafia,” he asked.Surveys and govt reports put the numbers differently. An MCG survey in 2017 identified 4,156 illegal structures within this belt. Officials estimate the number has since roughly doubled.Older govt data, including in the submissions made to the high court, had put total structures at 14,154, while a more recent MCG report flagged over 5,000 unauthorised structures and more than 190 ongoing construction sites in the zone.Punjab and Haryana high court had previously held that the 900-metre strip must remain free of urbanisation, and found that authorities allowed illegal construction to proliferate there. The court described the depot as a strategic installation where national interest could not be compromised.But govt action has repeatedly cut against this position. In 2015, Haryana filed an affidavit before the high court seeking to reduce the restricted zone from 900 to 300 metres.In 2016, the urban local bodies department approved temporary water connections for families in the 900-metre zone, citing the difficulty of removing thousands of residents.In 2017, authorities were directed to clear encroachments within a tighter 300-metre radius. A subsequent survey found 3,346 structures there, and the high court ordered their removal.MCG sealed several under-construction buildings last month, but a follow-up visit found many had been de-sealed and construction resumed. Hundreds of buildings are currently under construction in the zone.Residents describe a parallel civic ecosystem that has grown alongside the illegal settlement. A Sheetla Colony resident of about a decade alleged that local politicians and officials encouraged poor families to invest in construction there. “They help residents get voter cards and then use them as a vote bank during elections,” he said.A woman living in the area said residents have long been promised regularisation. “They help us get water and electricity connections. Roads have been built and sewerage laid,” she said.Another resident alleged that development tenders issued for adjoining areas are, in practice, executed inside the restricted zone: “Tenders are issued for development work in adjoining areas, but the actual work is carried out inside the 900-metre zone,” this person said.The issue has remained politically live. During the 2024 assembly campaign, Gurgaon MLA Mukesh Sharma listed resolving the zone’s problems among his priorities.In June 2026, Sharma met defence minister Rajnath Singh to seek the Centre’s intervention, citing the impact of the restrictions on civic works, property registrations and statutory approvals in the affected localities.A similar situation has played out near Faridabad Air Force Station in Dabua, where illegal construction within the restricted zone has been before Punjab and Haryana high court for over 15 years.The Centre notified a 100-metre restricted belt around the station in Jan 2010 under Works of Defence Act, prohibiting construction in the area. The matter reached the high court the same year through petitions seeking removal of illegal structures and action against officials responsible.In 2012, the court directed Faridabad Municipal Corporation to act against the illegal structures. By 2017, authorities estimated around 5,000 houses could be affected, and a 2018 survey identified 2,717 buildings within the 100-metre belt.Notices were issued to occupants, and authorities were directed to prevent further construction and transactions, but large populated colonies remain, with the issue still mired in legal and administrative hurdles.An area originally meant to stay free of urbanisation to protect a defence installation has become one of the city’s most densely populated pockets — serviced, in part, by the same civic machinery meant to keep it clear.With construction still underway, the unresolved question is not how the colonies came up, but how thousands of structures have been allowed to remain, expand and receive civic infrastructure inside a decades-old security zone.
Article Summary: The 900-metre restricted zone around Indian Air Force’s ammunition depot in old Gurgaon has been almost entirely built over. Supreme Court on Tuesday criticised state officials for colluding with local land sharks to allow this encroachment. Fifteen illegal colonies have come up in the belt over the years.

Article Title: Another Gurgaon shocker: 2 killed, 2 critical as DU student’s speeding car mows down 4 near Shriram Chowk
Article Text:
Two workers were killed and two others critically injured after a speeding white car crashed into a group of four workers Image Credit: TOI

GURGAON: Two workers were killed and two others critically injured after a speeding white car crashed into a group of four workers carrying out roadside metal grille installation work near Shriram Chowk on the Dwarka Expressway in the early hours of Thursday.The accident took place at around 2.30am when the car, which was travelling from the Delhi side, hit the workers working along the expressway.The driver of the car, identified as 20-year-old, a Delhi University student Vedan Khanna, was also injured in the crash. The collision was so severe that two of the workers died at the spot, while two others sustained serious injuries.Khanna is a resident of Indiabulls Enigma in Sector 110, Gurgaon. After receiving initial treatment, he was referred to Fortis Hospital for further treatment.Following the crash, the injured workers were taken to a nearby private hospital for treatment. After being informed, cops from Bajghera police station reached the spot. The Delhi number car was also impounded.Police have registered a case of rash and negligent driving causing death, at Bajghera police station.According to preliminary information, the speeding car, bearing registration number DL7CT-3165, allegedly went out of control and crashed into the workers at the site.The impact was severe, killing Bijendra, aged around 60, and Pappu Singh, also around 58 on the spot. Both deceased were residents of Bulandshahr in Uttar Pradesh.Two other workers, identified as Satish Chand (45) and Ram Kumar (28), sustained serious injuries in the accident. They were rushed to hospital after the incident for treatment.
Article Summary: Two workers were killed and two others critically injured after a speeding white car crashed into a group of four workers. The collision was so severe that two of the workers died at the spot, while two others sustained serious injuries. The driver of the car, identified as 20-year-old, a Delhi University student Vedan Khanna, was also injured.

Article Title: DU teacher assaulted during DUSU campaign, faculty threaten election boycott
Article Text:
A DU teacher faced assault by a student campaigner. Faculty members protested the incident and threatened to boycott election duties.





NEW DELHI: A Delhi University teacher was allegedly assaulted by a student campaigning for the Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) elections at Motilal Nehru College (Evening) on Wednesday, triggering a protest by faculty members and a threat to boycott election duties.The alleged assault came as the final day of campaigning was marred by clashes and altercations at several DU campuses.Faculty members gathered at the college after the alleged incident and demanded action against the student.A teacher said the faculty member who was allegedly attacked sustained serious injuries and was receiving medical attention.“A DUSU campaigner beat a faculty member. He is grievously injured and is receiving medical attention,” the teacher said.The teacher said faculty members were considering filing an FIR and boycotting election-related duties in protest against the incident.“Teachers are protesting against the DUSU election. We will also be filing an FIR and boycott any election duties. Students need to understand the boundary. Faculty members cannot be beaten up,” the teacher said.Faculty members were not immediately sure which student organisation the alleged campaigner represented.The incident took place on the day campaigning for the DUSU elections concluded. Polling is scheduled for September 18, with counting on September 19.The alleged assault was reported amid a wider flare-up of tensions across DU on the final day of campaigning. At North Campus, a clash broke out outside Law Centre-I after an argument over the removal of campaign banners.ABVP alleged that three of its members were injured, including two with head injuries and another with a hand fracture. Videos circulating on social media showed groups of students exchanging blows and damaged vehicles, though the videos did not independently establish how the clash began.At South Campus, faculty members at Motilal Nehru College said campaigners clashed with teachers while trying to enter the premises and that several teachers were injured.NSUI separately alleged that ABVP-linked workers attacked one of its tribal student workers outside the college, a charge denied by ABVP.Another clash was reported at Sri Aurobindo College, while altercations were reported from other colleges as well.Faculty members later staged a protest against DUSU campaigners. A staff association meeting continued till late evening to decide on filing a police complaint.The developments have raised concerns among faculty members over the conduct of student campaigning and safety on campus ahead of the September 18 DUSU polls.
Article Summary: A Delhi University teacher was allegedly assaulted by a student campaigning for the Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) elections. Faculty members protested the incident and threatened to boycott election duties. The alleged assault came as the final day of campaigning was marred by clashes.

Article Title: After meeting govt delegation, Manoj Jarange calls off hunger strike on 20th day of agitation, gives govt another three months
Article Text:
Manoj Jarange ended his 20-day hunger strike after government talks.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange on Thursday morning called off his indefinite hunger strike on its 20th day after a government delegation held talks with him at Patoda in Beed district and sought three months to address his key demands. This was Jarange’s 11th agitation over the past three years.Cabinet ministers Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil and Dada Bhuse, along with BJP MLA from Ashti Suresh Dhas and BJP MLC Prasad Lad, reached Patoda around 5.40am to discuss Jarange’s demands on behalf of the govt. Following the talks, Jarange announced that he was suspending his fast for 90 days, saying there had been positive discussions on his five main demands.Jarange said the suspension of the hunger strike did not mean the end of his agitation. He gave the government three months to issue the necessary government resolution and implement the Gazetteer-related measures. He also demanded a written assurance that not a single record would be deleted from the nearly 58 lakh records identified in the process of establishing Maratha-Kunbi links.“If the government betrays us, we will go to Mumbai,” Jarange warned, while appealing to over 1 lakh of his supporters who according to him had travelled towards Mumbai, to return home.He said he was prepared to trust the government for three months following the discussions at Patoda.Before announcing the suspension of his fast, Jarange also said Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis was not his enemy and indicated that he would continue to maintain affection for Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, while making it clear that he would not compromise on the demands of the Maratha community.After ending his fast, Jarange left Patoda for a private hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city, where he had been undergoing treatment periodically for the past three years.
Article Summary: Manoj Jarange ended his 20-day hunger strike after government talks. Jarange said the suspension of the hunger strike did not mean the end of his agitation. He gave the government three months to issue the necessary government resolution and implement the Gazetteer-related measures.

Article Title: UP man beheads sleeping wife over ‘affair’, walks into police station
Article Text:
A man allegedly beheaded his sleeping wife in Hardoi over suspected infidelity.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think should be done to prevent domestic abuse? Stricter laws and penalties More awareness campaigns Support services for victims 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





LUCKNOW: Suspecting his wife of having an affair, a man allegedly beheaded her while she was asleep at their rented house in Hardoi’s Islamnagar Tiliya locality early Wednesday, police said.The accused, identified as Parvez (34), was arrested after he reportedly walked into a police station and surrendered.The victim, Nagma (28), had been married to Parvez for nearly 12 years. According to police, the couple’s relationship had been strained for several months, with Parvez allegedly suspecting his wife of being in contact with another man on the phone. Frequent arguments reportedly took place over the issue.Investigators said Nagma was sleeping when Parvez allegedly attacked her with a sharp-edged weapon. Police said he repeatedly assaulted her before severing her head.The couple had been living in a rented house for the past one-and-a-half months after Parvez sold his ancestral property.Nagma’s sister, Sabbo, claimed that she had been subjected to prolonged physical abuse and threats by her husband. She alleged that Parvez had repeatedly threatened to slit Nagma’s throat in the days leading up to the murder.The family also alleged that some of Parvez’s relatives were present in the house when the crime took place.Nagma’s mother, Zahida, alleged that her daughter had faced repeated harassment and intimidation from her husband and in-laws.Police have sent the body for postmortem and launched an investigation. Officers are questioning Parvez, examining the family’s allegations, and attempting to recover the weapon allegedly used in the crime.
Article Summary: The accused, identified as Parvez (34), was arrested after he reportedly walked into a police station and surrendered. The victim, Nagma (28), had been married to Parvez for nearly 12 years. Parvez allegedly suspecting his wife of being in contact with another man on the phone.

Article Title: Days after PM Modi’s school friend gets relief in land dispute, Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancels construction permission to BJP MLA’s company
Article Text:
Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancelled construction permission for Seven Eleven company.





BHAYANDER: The Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation on Wednesday cancelled the construction permission granted to Seven Eleven company, days after BJP MLA Narendra Mehta announced that his company would relinquish possession of the disputed land following the matter being taken up with Prime Minister Narendra Modi In another development, additional tehsildar Nilesh Gaund allowed a petition filed by 81-year-old Asgarali Vohra and ruled against Seven Eleven and other respondents. The order is expected to clear the way for Vohra’s name to be entered in the land records for the property currently in the possession of Seven Eleven, which had fenced off the plot with metal sheets.Vohra had alleged that Mehta and Swayam Builders had illegally encroached on the land at Navghar in Bhayander. He had been pursuing the dispute for around 15 years.On September 8, Vohra approached PM Modi, whom he described as his childhood friend from B N School in Vadnagar in Gujarat, and sought his intervention in the dispute. Soon after, Mehta announced that he would relinquish possession of the property and withdraw a complaint filed against Vohra.On Wednesday, Mehta issued a statement denying that he or his company had cheated anyone.He said the disputed land had been sold to Vohra in 1989 by Renol Lobo and five others. Lobo and the others later sold the land to Swayam Builders in 2011, he said.Mehta further claimed that Seven Eleven had purchased the property through duly registered transactions from Joseph Fernandes and Mukesh Parekh. He said the company decided to return the land to Mukesh Parekh and Mervin Fernandes after a dispute arose over the property.The BJP MLA maintained that surrendering possession and cancelling the transaction was a decision taken to end the dispute and did not amount to an admission of wrongdoing.
Article Summary: Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancelled construction permission for Seven Eleven company. BJP MLA Narendra Mehta announced that his company would relinquish possession of the disputed land. In another development, additional tehsildar Nilesh Gaund allowed a petition filed by 81-year-old Asgarali Vohra and ruled against Seven Eleven.

Article Title: Another hit-and-run in Delhi-NCR: Man collecting birthday cake hit by speeding SUV in Greater Noida, suffers spine fracture
Article Text:
A speeding car struck a pedestrian near Ek Murti Chowk, causing serious injuries





NOIDA: A 32-year-old man suffered several fractures in a hit-and-run accident at Ek Murti Chowk in Greater Noida earlier this month. A video of the accident recorded by a rear-view camera of a car shows that the collision impact flung the man into the air.Police have arrested the driver, a 24-year-old management student, on Sept 14 and impounded the car.According to a complaint filed by the victim, Himanshu Rai, at the Bisrakh police station, the accident took place at around 4.35 am on Sept 5. He told the cops, “It was my birthday, so after work my wife and I had gone out.”He collected a pre-ordered cake from a bakery and was crossing the road at the chowk when a white SUV, driven at high speed, rammed him.“The car hit me at what appeared to be a speed of over 100 km per hour and drove away. The way the car was being driven, it seemed that the driver might have been under the influence of alcohol,” he said.People in the vicinity rushed to his aid and took him to a hospital for treatment.The man sustained fractures to his legs, hand and knees, besides suffering a fracture to his spine. He is currently undergoing treatment at the hospital.Police subsequently traced the vehicle and initiated action against the driver, Priyanshu. The Tata Punch allegedly involved in the accident was taken into custody.A case has been registered against him under BNS sections 125(b) (act endangering life or personal safety) and 281 (rash driving).The accident comes at the heel of a hit and run incident in Gurgaon where a biker was chased down by a group of men on Golf Course Road.Kalyan Bainsla (33), who rammed his car into Shivani Chauhan’s bike and caused her to fall in the middle of fast-moving traffic on Golf Course Road Sunday morning, was arrested at Dausa in Rajasthan on Tuesday.A video from her bike’s camera that Chauhan uploaded online showed her being knocked down near Sector 55-56 Rapid Metro station after the car repeatedly tried to get alongside her bike.Her Aprilia RS 457 slid across the road, while traffic sped past her.Bainsla’s cousin Lovneesh (32), who was in the Maruti Ciaz with him on Sunday, was arrested too. After examining the video of the crash that Shivani shared, police have added the attempt to murder charge in the FIR against Bainsla.“He caused the collision deliberately from the side. He had an intention to kill her,” DCP (east) Sandeep Kumar said
Article Summary: A 32-year-old man suffered several fractures in a hit-and-run accident at Ek Murti Chowk in Greater Noida earlier this month. A video of the accident recorded by a rear-view camera of a car shows that the collision impact flung the man into the air. The incident comes at the heel of a hit and run incident in Gurgaon where a biker was chased down.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos continues to be the richest man of the US state, he relocated three years ago, and where billionaires 'fleeing' California are moving to
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos moved to Florida in 2023, three years later he remains Florida’s richest billionaire as fortune jumps to …

Why Jeff Bezos moved from Seattle to Miami

Jeff Bezos says leaving Seattle was emotional

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos remains the richest billionaire in Florida nearly three years after he moved to the state from Seattle. Forbes’ recently updated list of the 400 richest people in America ranks Jeff Bezos No. 2 overall, behind Tesla and SpaceX co-founder Elon Musk . Bezos’ estimated net worth has also jumped sharply over the past year, rising from $241 billion to $378 billion, according to Forbes. Notably, Florida is the state that billionaires are reportedly fleeing California to escape a crippling tax hike. Jeff Bezos moved to Miami in 2023 after nearly three decades in Seattle, Washington. He said he wanted to be closer to his parents, who had moved back to Florida, while also pointing to the growing role of his space company Blue Origin in Florida.Jacksonville Jaguars owner Shad Khan is another major billionaire in Florida. With a net worth of $16.5 billion, he ranks No. 8 in Florida and No. 70 overall on the Forbes list. President Donald Trump is also among the 48 billionaires on the list with an estimated net worth of $7 billion.Jeff Bezos announced his move in November 2023 through an Instagram post. “Seattle has been my home since 1994 when I started Amazon out of my garage,” Bezos wrote. He said his parents had recently moved back to Miami, where he lived when he was younger.“I want to be close to my parents, and Lauren and I love Miami,” he added.Bezos also said Blue Origin’s operations were increasingly shifting to Cape Canaveral, making the move to Florida more practical. “For all that, I’m planning to return to Miami, leaving the Pacific Northwest,” he wrote.Seattle had been Jeff Bezos’ home for longer than any other place in his life. He said the decision to leave was exciting but also emotional. “I’ve lived in Seattle longer than I’ve lived anywhere else and have so many amazing memories here,” Bezos wrote.“As exciting as the move is, it’s an emotional decision for me. Seattle, you will always have a piece of my heart.”
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos moved to Miami in 2023 after nearly three decades in Seattle, Washington. Forbes’ recently updated list of the 400 richest people in America ranks Jeff Bezos No. 2 overall. Bezos’ estimated net worth has also jumped sharply over the past year, rising from $241 billion to $378 billion.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.

Article Title: ‘Result of criminal conduct’: HC laments ‘tragic’ loss of lives in building collapse
Article Text:
New Delhi:





The Sept 6 building collapse in Satya Niketan that claimed seven lives, including those of students, was not an “ordinary mishap” but a result of “criminal conduct”, Delhi high court said Wednesday.A bench of Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said these students came from small towns to the capital with “a lot of hopes and dreams” of building a life, but these were “shattered” due to the “callous and criminal conduct” of certain persons.“Very tragic,” the court observed about the incident, after additional solicitor general Chetan Sharma said that authorities have now taken several steps, including proactive mapping and earmarking of land and other facilities for students in Delhi.The bench’s oral remarks came while it was hearing a fresh plea seeking that the authorities maintain an online platform to indicate availability of hostels for students in the city. The court said the PIL will be heard along with another pending petition on the matter on Sept 25.The bench, though, noted that the issue of lack of hostel facilities in the city is not a “new phenomenon”. It said, “Who doesn’t know the problem of hostels? Students are flocking to Delhi for higher education...for the last 20-25 years in the hope that they will build their career. See what has happened.”The court earlier ordered a high-level MCD inquiry into the incident and made it clear that govt could not evade responsibility. It had said not only was it unfortunate, but it also evoked deep concern about inadequate housing facilities, including hostels run by Delhi University or govt, lack of safety and security of students and not-so-adequate measures employed by MCD and other authorities to regulate such PG facilities in Delhi.
Article Summary: The Sept 6 building collapse in Satya Niketan claimed seven lives, including those of students. A bench of Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said these students came from small towns to the capital with “a lot of hopes and dreams” of building a life.
